Device Configuration

Teltonika Configurator — Full Tab Reference

A field-by-field walkthrough of the Teltonika Configurator, covering the full FMB640 tab set (connection/protocol basics through scenario-based event logic and I/O mapping) plus the FMC650's CAN & Tachograph tabs (FMS-standard vehicle data, raw CAN decoding, and digital tachograph integration).

Devices: FMB640, FMC650 Configurator: v4.37.1.0 / v4.41.0.0 Category: Device Configuration

Part 1 — FMB640 core configuration

Device note: Sections 1–11 were captured against an FMB640 profile (Configurator v4.37.1.0). Tab availability and field behavior are broadly consistent across the FMB6xx / FMx6xx families.

1. System

Core device behavior: sleep modes, movement/GNSS sourcing, protocol version, record handling, static navigation filtering, ignition detection, and time sync. This is usually the first tab to review on a fresh configuration.

System tab — Sleep Mode, System Settings, Protocol Settings, Ignition Source, Records Settings, Static Navigation Settings, and Time Synchronization.

Sleep Mode

Controls whether and how the device powers down non-essential modules to save battery/power when the vehicle is stationary and ignition is off.

\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
DisableDevice never enters a low-power state; GNSS and modem stay fully active at all times.
GPS SleepOnly the GNSS receiver is put to sleep; GSM/GPRS stays online.
Deep SleepBoth GNSS and GSM modules power down; device wakes on movement/ignition/timer.
Online Deep SleepLike Deep Sleep, but the GPRS connection to the server is kept alive so the device stays reachable.
Timeout (min)Idle time (no movement, ignition off) before the selected sleep mode engages.

System Settings

Defines what the device treats as 'movement' and where it pulls GNSS, odometer, and speed data from — critical for accurate trip/idle detection and mileage reporting.

\n\n\n\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Movement SourceWhich input (Ignition, Accelerometer, GNSS, or CAN Speed) the device uses to decide the vehicle is moving.
GNSS SourceSatellite constellations enabled for positioning — GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou (multiple can be active together for faster/ more accurate fixes).
Battery Charge ModeWhen the internal backup battery is charged — On Need (as required) or only After Ignition ON.
Analog Input Value RangeVoltage range (10V or 30V) the AIN1–AIN2 inputs are calibrated to read.
AIN4/DOUT4 ModeWhether physical pin 4 is used as an analog input (Ain4) or a digital output (DOUT4).
Analog Input Value Range 3-4Voltage range (10V or 30V) for AIN3/AIN4, set independently from AIN1/AIN2.
Odometer Source SettingsWhere the device pulls mileage from: GPS-calculated distance, LVCAN (vehicle CAN bus), FMS, or KLINE — matters for GPS-vs-CAN odometer reconciliation work.
Speed Source SettingsSame idea as odometer source, but for reported vehicle speed: GPS, LVCAN, FMS, or KLINE.

Protocol Settings

Chooses the data protocol the device uses to package and send AVL records to the server.

\n
FieldWhat it does
Codec 8Standard Teltonika data protocol; supports up to ~50 elements per record — used for most integrations.
Codec 8 ExtendedExtended-field version of Codec 8, needed when I/O elements or record payloads exceed what standard Codec 8 supports.

Records Settings

Controls how and when the device commits records to memory/SD and how it behaves around link and time-sync issues.

\n\n\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Records Saving/Sending Without TSWhether the device will save/send records that don't yet have a valid timestamp — After Position Fix (wait for GNSS fix) or Always (send regardless).
Open Link Timeout (s)How long the device waits for the server connection to open before giving up and retrying.
Response Timeout (s)How long the device waits for a server acknowledgment after sending a record before considering the send failed.
Sort ByOrder records are transmitted in from the buffer — Newest first or Oldest first.
Save Records ToWhere AVL records are stored — Internal Memory or SD Card (SD card extends buffering capacity significantly).
Ping ModeWhether the device sends an empty Codec 12 'ping' packet to keep the connection alive during idle periods.
Network Ping Timeout (min)Interval between keep-alive pings when Ping Mode is enabled.

Static Navigation Settings

Filters out GNSS position 'jitter' — small, false movement readings that occur while the vehicle is genuinely stationary (common cause of phantom trips in reports).

\n
FieldWhat it does
Static NavigationEnable/disable the jitter filter.
Static Navigation Deactivation SourceWhat condition is required to exit static (stationary) mode and start accepting position updates again — Movement OR Ignition, Movement only, Ignition only, or Movement AND Ignition.

Ignition Source

Defines how the device determines ignition state — foundational for trip start/stop, idle time, and most reporting logic.

\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Ignition SettingsSelects the physical/logical source used to detect ignition: a Digital Input (1–4), Movement, or Power Voltage.
High Voltage / Low Voltage (mV)When Power Voltage is the ignition source, these thresholds define the voltage range considered 'ignition on' vs 'ignition off' — useful when there's no clean ignition-wired DIN.
Movement Start Delay (s)Debounce delay before the device confirms movement has started, to avoid false positives from small jolts.
Movement Stop Delay (s)Debounce delay before the device confirms the vehicle has actually stopped.

Time Synchronization

Keeps the device clock accurate, which underpins every timestamped record it produces.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Synchronization SettingsSource used to sync time — GNSS only, NITZ+NTP, NTP only, or NITZ only (network-provided time).
NTP Sync TimeoutHow long the device waits for an NTP server response before falling back.
NTP Server 1 / NTP Server 2Primary and backup NTP server addresses (defaults to Teltonika's own NTP server and pool.ntp.org).
Why this tab matters for investigations: Movement Source, Ignition Source, and Static Navigation settings directly affect trip detection accuracy — misconfiguration here is a common root cause of inflated idle time or phantom short trips in client reports.
\n

2. GPRS

Everything related to the device's cellular data connection: data caps, SIM/APN configuration for dual-SIM units, the primary and backup servers it reports to, and FOTA (firmware-over-the-air) settings.

GPRS tab — GPRS Limits, SIM1/SIM2 GPRS Settings, Server #1/#2 Settings, and FOTA WEB Settings.

GPRS Limits

Optional data usage caps to protect against runaway SIM billing.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
GPRS LimitsEnable/disable data usage limiting.
Home Limit (MB)Monthly data cap while on the home network.
Roaming Limit (MB)Monthly data cap while roaming (typically set lower given roaming data cost).

SIM1 / SIM2 GPRS Settings

APN configuration for each SIM slot — required for the device to establish a mobile data session at all. Dual-SIM units use these for failover or region switching.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
GPRS ContextEnable/disable the data context for that SIM.
APNAccess Point Name provided by the mobile carrier.
APN Username / APN PasswordCarrier-issued credentials, if the APN requires authentication.

Server #1 Settings

The primary telemetry server the device streams AVL records to.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
DomainHostname or IP address of the receiving server.
PortTCP/UDP port the server listens on.
ProtocolTransport protocol — TCP (reliable, used almost universally) or UDP.

Server #2 Settings

An optional secondary destination, useful for redundancy or sending the same data to two platforms.

\n
FieldWhat it does
Backup Server ModeDisable, Backup (only used if Server #1 fails), or Duplicate (sends every record to both servers simultaneously).
Backup Server Domain / Port / ProtocolConnection details for the second server, same meaning as Server #1's fields.

FOTA WEB Settings

Controls whether the device checks in with Teltonika's Firmware-Over-The-Air platform for remote firmware/config management.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
StatusEnable/disable FOTA WEB check-ins.
Domain / PortTeltonika's FOTA WEB endpoint (defaults to fm.teltonika.lt:5000).
Period (min)How often the device checks in with FOTA WEB.
Field tip: If a device shows connectivity but never reports data, check APN correctness first, then confirm Server #1's Domain/Port/Protocol match what the receiving platform actually expects.
\n

3. Data Acquisition

Defines exactly when the device generates a new AVL record and how often it sends data — split by vehicle state (On Stop vs Moving) and by network condition (Home / Roaming / Unknown). Also covers on-demand tracking bursts.

Data Acquisition tab — On Stop and Moving record/send rules by network state, plus On Demand Tracking.

On Stop

Record and send behavior while the vehicle is stationary — generally relaxed intervals to conserve data, since nothing is changing.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Min Period (s)Minimum time between generated records while stopped (e.g. 3600s = one record per hour).
Min Saved RecordsMinimum number of buffered records before the device attempts a send.
Send Period (s)How often the device attempts to transmit buffered records to the server.

Moving

Record and send behavior while the vehicle is in motion — tighter thresholds for higher-resolution tracking.

\n\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Min Period (s)Minimum time between records while moving.
Min Distance (m)Minimum distance traveled before a new record is generated, even if the time threshold hasn't elapsed.
Min Angle (°)Minimum heading change that triggers a new record — captures turns even during a straight-line time/distance gap.
Min Speed Delta (km/h)Minimum speed change that triggers a new record — captures hard acceleration/braking events.
Min Saved RecordsMinimum buffered records before attempting a send while moving.
Send Period (s)How often the device attempts to transmit while moving.

Network-state columns (Home / Roaming / Unknown)

Both On Stop and Moving rule sets are defined three times, once per network state, so behavior (and data cost) can be tuned differently when a vehicle crosses into roaming.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
HomeRules applied while on the SIM's home network.
RoamingRules applied while roaming — commonly loosened to cut data costs.
UnknownRules applied when the device can't determine network state.

On Demand Tracking

A short burst of high-frequency tracking that can be triggered manually or by an input, useful for temporarily following a specific vehicle closely (e.g. active investigation).

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Period (s)Interval between records during the on-demand tracking burst.
Duration (s)Total length of time the burst lasts before reverting to normal acquisition rules.
Activation byWhich digital or analog inputs (DIN1–3, AIN1–4) can trigger the burst.
\n

4. SMS \ Call Settings

Configures remote SMS command access, how the device handles incoming calls, hands-free call triggering from digital inputs, and the authorized number lists that gate all of the above.

SMS \\ Call Settings tab — SMS Commands, Incoming Call Settings, Hands Free Call Settings, Authorized Numbers, and GSM Predefined Numbers.

SMS Commands

Credentials and formatting for sending the device text-based configuration/status commands.

\n
FieldWhat it does
Login / PasswordOptional credentials required as a prefix in SMS commands sent to the device, for security.
SMS Event Time ZoneTime zone applied to timestamps included in outgoing SMS event notifications.

Incoming Call Settings

What the device does when it receives a phone call.

\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Do Nothing (BT HF)Ignores the call at the device level (a connected Bluetooth hands-free unit may still handle it).
HangupAutomatically rejects the incoming call.
Report PositionAnswers by sending its current position back via SMS, without opening audio.
SPY CallSilently answers the call and opens the microphone (audio monitoring) — used for authorized SPY/listen-in scenarios only.
Auto Answer (HF)Automatically answers the call as a hands-free voice call.

Hands Free Call Settings

Lets a digital input trigger an outbound hands-free call automatically — e.g. a panic button wired to a DIN.

\n
FieldWhat it does
Din 1-4 Call TriggerEnable/disable an outbound call being placed when that digital input activates.
GSM NumberWhich number from the GSM Predefined Numbers list is dialed when that DIN triggers.

Authorized Numbers

A whitelist of phone numbers permitted to send SMS commands to or call the device — a core security control.

FieldWhat it does
List (1-10+)Phone numbers entered manually, or bulk-loaded/exported via CSV.

GSM Predefined Numbers

A separate number list used specifically as call targets for the Hands Free Call Settings triggers above.

FieldWhat it does
List (1-10+)Phone numbers entered manually, or bulk-loaded/exported via CSV.
Security note: Leaving Authorized Numbers empty typically means the device accepts SMS commands from any number — always populate this list on production devices.
\n

5. SMS Events

Maps specific I/O element (AVL ID) state changes to an outbound SMS notification, sent to a chosen number with custom text — e.g. texting a manager when a door sensor or panic input fires.

SMS Events tab — SMS Events AVL ID, SMS Events Number, and SMS Event Text, configured as matched rows.

SMS Events AVL ID

The I/O element ID being watched for this event row. When that element's value changes/triggers, the corresponding row's SMS fires.

FieldWhat it does
AVL ID (1-10 rows)Numeric ID of the monitored I/O parameter (e.g. a digital input, ignition, GPS Odometer, etc. — per the device's AVL ID list).

SMS Events Number

Which recipient number (drawn from the number lists elsewhere in the config) receives the notification for that row.

FieldWhat it does
Number (1-10 rows)Destination phone number for that event row, selected from a dropdown of configured numbers.

SMS Event Text

The literal message body sent for that row's event.

FieldWhat it does
Text (1-10 rows)Free-text message content, importable/exportable via CSV for bulk setup across many devices.
How the rows relate: Row 1 of AVL ID, Number, and Text together define one complete event rule; up to 10 independent event rules can be active at once.
\n

6. GSM Operators

Controls which mobile network operators the device is allowed to roam onto (per SIM), and a global blacklist of operators to avoid entirely — useful for cross-border fleets where certain roaming partners are unreliable or expensive.

GSM Operators tab — SIM1 Roaming Operator List, SIM2 Roaming/Home Operator List, and Operator Black List.

SIM1 Roaming Operator List

A preferred/allowed list of operator codes (MCC+MNC) SIM1 may connect to while roaming.

FieldWhat it does
List (1-20 rows)Operator numeric codes, entered manually or via CSV import/export.

SIM2 Roaming/Home Operator List

Same concept as above, applied to SIM2 — covers both home and roaming operator selection for the second SIM slot.

FieldWhat it does
List (1-20 rows)Operator numeric codes, entered manually or via CSV import/export.

Operator Black List

Operator codes the device will never connect to, regardless of SIM — takes priority over the allow lists above.

FieldWhat it does
List (1-20 rows)Operator numeric codes to exclude entirely, entered manually or via CSV import/export.
Use case: Cross-border fleets (e.g. regional freight) commonly use this tab to blacklist known-poor roaming partners and pin devices to reliable operators near border regions.
\n

7. Features

A set of independent "scenario" modules that generate special-purpose event records — driving behavior scoring, over-speeding, jamming detection, remote relay control, immobilizer logic, iButton read notifications, pulse counting, and short-burst data uploads over satellite (SBD).

Features tab — Green Driving, Over Speeding, Jamming, DOUT Control Via Call, Immobilizer, iButton Read Notification, Impulse Counters, and Short Burst Data Settings.
Scenario Settings pattern: Most Features/Accelerometer Features scenarios share the same first block — Disable, Low Priority, High Priority, Panic Priority — which both enables the scenario and sets the priority level attached to the event record it generates (higher priority records are sent ahead of routine data when the buffer is under pressure).

Green Driving

Scores harsh acceleration, braking, and cornering events using accelerometer/GNSS data — the basis for eco-driving/driver-behavior reports.

\n\n\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Output ControlOptional digital output (DOUT) pulsed when a harsh-driving event is detected — e.g. to trigger an in-cab buzzer.
GNSS / AccelerometerWhich sensor source calculates the G-force values — GNSS-derived speed changes or the onboard Accelerometer.
GNSS Algorithm A1 / Accelerometer Algorithm A1The specific calculation algorithm used for that source.
Advanced Eco DrivingEnables the granular Max Acceleration / Max Braking / Max Cornering thresholds below instead of a single generic sensitivity.
Max Acceleration/Braking/Cornering (m/s²)G-force thresholds above which an event is logged for each behavior type.
DOUT ON/OFF Duration (ms)Pulse length of the linked output when a harsh event fires.
Send SMS To / SMS TextOptional SMS alert sent to a chosen number when a Green Driving event occurs.

Over Speeding

Flags when the vehicle exceeds a configured speed limit.

\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Max Speed (km/h)Speed threshold that triggers the event.
Output ControlOptional DOUT pulsed on an over-speed event.
DOUT ON/OFF Duration (ms)Pulse length for the linked output.
Send SMS To / SMS TextOptional SMS alert sent when the vehicle exceeds the limit.

Jamming

Detects GSM signal jamming (a common tactic in cargo theft) so it can be logged and alerted on even while communications are being actively disrupted.

\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Output ControlOptional DOUT triggered when jamming is detected.
SensitivityLow / Normal / High detection sensitivity.
DOUT ON/OFF Duration, DOUT Hold Delay (s)Timing behavior of the linked output during a jamming event.
Time Until Jamming Event Detection (s)How long sustained interference must persist before it's classified as a jamming event, filtering out brief signal dips.

DOUT Control Via Call

Lets an authorized phone call remotely toggle a digital output — commonly used for remote engine cut relays or gate/lock control.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Digital Output ControlWhich DOUT (1–3) is toggled by an incoming authorized call.
DOUT Deactivation SettingsWhich digital input (or None) can deactivate the output afterward, giving a manual local override.
Duration Timeout (s)How long the output stays active before automatically releasing, as a safety fallback.

Immobilizer

A dedicated engine-immobilization scenario, typically paired with an iButton reader — the vehicle can be blocked from starting unless an authorized iButton is presented.

\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Output ControlDOUT used to interrupt the starter/fuel circuit.
iButton List CheckWhether presented iButtons are validated against the configured iButton List before allowing the vehicle to start.
Ignition TMO (s)Time allowed after ignition-on for a valid iButton to be presented before immobilization engages.
Authorization TMO (s)Time window during which a scanned iButton is considered valid for that start attempt.
Send SMS To / SMS TextOptional alert when the immobilizer engages.

iButton Read Notification

Notifies when any iButton is read at the reader, independent of the Immobilizer feature — useful for driver-identification logging.

\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Output ControlOptional DOUT pulsed on a successful iButton read.
DOUT ON Duration (ms)Pulse length for the linked output.
iButton List CheckingWhether the read is validated against the configured iButton list.
Depend On IgnitionWhether the notification only fires while ignition is on.

Impulse Counters Settings

Configures two independent pulse counters (e.g. for fuel flow meters or PTO cycle counting) and which physical input feeds each one.

FieldWhat it does
Impulse Counter 1/2 InputSelects the DIN or AIN pin whose pulses are counted, or None to disable that counter.

Short Burst Data Settings

Configuration for Short Burst Data (SBD) — used with satellite modem add-ons (TSM232) to send compact records when there's no cellular coverage.

\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
TSM232Enable/disable the satellite SBD module integration.
Save/Send Period (min)How often SBD records are generated/sent while outside cellular coverage.
SBD Upload LimitData cap per transmission window (satellite bandwidth is expensive and limited).
SBD IO SourceWhich digital/analog inputs and outputs are included in the compact SBD payload.
Return FlowWhether the satellite channel also accepts inbound commands/config back to the device.
\n

8. Accelerometer Features

Motion-sensor-driven event scenarios that don't depend on GNSS alone — excessive idling, unauthorized towing, crash detection, and the accelerometer's own auto-calibration behavior. Central to fuel/accident-investigation work.

Accelerometer Features tab — Excessive Idling, Towing Detection, Crash Detection, and Accelerometer Autocalibration.
Scenario Settings pattern: Most Features/Accelerometer Features scenarios share the same first block — Disable, Low Priority, High Priority, Panic Priority — which both enables the scenario and sets the priority level attached to the event record it generates (higher priority records are sent ahead of routine data when the buffer is under pressure).

Excessive Idling

Flags when the engine/ignition stays on without the vehicle moving for longer than expected — a key input for fuel-waste and driver-behavior reporting.

\n\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Time To Stopped (s)How long the vehicle must be stationary with ignition on before idling starts being counted.
Time To Moving (s)How long continuous movement must be detected before the idling state is cleared.
Start/Stop Speed Threshold (km/h)Speed values used to distinguish 'stopped' from 'moving' for this scenario specifically.
Output ControlOptional DOUT pulsed when excessive idling is flagged.
DOUT ON/OFF Duration (ms)Pulse length for the linked output.
Send SMS To / SMS TextOptional SMS alert on an idling event.

Towing Detection

Flags movement detected by the accelerometer while ignition is off — the classic signature of a vehicle being towed or transported without authorization.

\n\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Activation Timeout (min)How long ignition must stay off before towing detection logic starts monitoring.
Event Timeout (s)Cooldown before a new towing event can be logged after one just fired.
Threshold (g)Minimum acceleration force that counts as movement for this scenario.
Angle (deg)Minimum tilt/orientation change also considered as evidence of towing.
Duration (ms)How long the triggering motion must be sustained before it's confirmed as a towing event (filters out bumps/vibration).
Make Call To / Send SMS To / SMS TextAlert channel(s) triggered when towing is detected — this scenario supports an automatic phone call in addition to SMS.

Crash Detection

Captures high-G impact events and can optionally record detailed accelerometer trace data around the moment of impact — directly feeds accident-reconstruction investigations.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Duration (ms) / Threshold (mg)The impact profile that qualifies as a crash: sustained G-force above the threshold for at least the duration.
Send SMS To / SMS Text / Make Call ToAlert channels triggered immediately on a detected crash.
Crash TraceDisable, Trace Changes (log the accelerometer delta around the event), or Trace Full (log the full raw accelerometer waveform) — Trace Full gives the richest reconstruction data but uses more memory/bandwidth.

Accelerometer Autocalibration

Keeps the accelerometer's reference orientation accurate as the device settles into its mounted position, and filters out gravity's constant contribution from motion readings.

\n
FieldWhat it does
Accelerometer Auto CalibrationEnable/disable automatic axis calibration after mounting.
Gravity FilterEnable/disable filtering of the constant 1g gravity vector from acceleration readings, so reported G-forces reflect vehicle motion only.
Why this tab matters for investigations: Crash Detection's Threshold/Duration pairing and Crash Trace setting directly determine how much usable evidence is available after an incident — Trace Full is worth enabling on vehicles where accident reconstruction is a realistic possibility.
\n

9. Auto Geofence

A single dynamic geofence that automatically forms around the vehicle's last stopping point, rather than a fixed zone you draw on a map (that's covered by Manual Geofence Settings/Zones instead). Useful for detecting unauthorized movement from a parked/depot location.

Auto Geofence tab — Scenario Settings, Generate Event, Activation Timeout, Radius, and Deactivate By options.
Scenario Settings pattern: Most Features/Accelerometer Features scenarios share the same first block — Disable, Low Priority, High Priority, Panic Priority — which both enables the scenario and sets the priority level attached to the event record it generates (higher priority records are sent ahead of routine data when the buffer is under pressure).

Auto Geofence

How the dynamic zone is generated and what deactivates it.

\n\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Eventual RecordsWhether entering/exiting the auto-generated zone produces a loggable event record.
Generate EventWhich crossing direction triggers the event — On Exit, On Entrance, or On Both.
Activation Timeout (s)How long the vehicle must remain stationary before the geofence circle is drawn around its current position.
Radius (m)Size of the auto-generated zone around that stopping point.
Deactivate ByWhat re-arms/clears the auto geofence so a new one can form at the next stop — Ignition, iButton, or Engine RPM.
Send SMS To / SMS TextOptional SMS alert when the auto geofence is crossed.
Auto vs Manual: Auto Geofence re-centers itself every time the vehicle parks; Manual Geofence Settings/Zones (separate tabs) are for fixed, named zones like depots, customer sites, or restricted regions.
\n

10. Trip \ Odometer

Defines what counts as a "trip" for reporting purposes, and a few odometer/eco-score related behaviors layered on top of trip detection.

Trip \\ Odometer tab — Trip Settings and Advanced Trip Settings.
Scenario Settings pattern: Most Features/Accelerometer Features scenarios share the same first block — Disable, Low Priority, High Priority, Panic Priority — which both enables the scenario and sets the priority level attached to the event record it generates (higher priority records are sent ahead of routine data when the buffer is under pressure).

Trip Settings

Core trip start/stop logic used to segment continuous GNSS/CAN data into discrete trips.

\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
ModeContinuous (trip data streamed throughout) or Between Records (trip summary generated only between saved records).
Start Speed (km/h)Minimum speed that counts as the vehicle actually starting to move, avoiding false trip starts from GNSS drift.
Ignition OFF Timeout (s)How long ignition must stay off before the trip is considered ended, allowing brief stops (e.g. traffic lights) to stay within one trip.
Send SMS To / SMS TextOptional SMS alert on trip start/stop.

Advanced Trip Settings

Secondary options tied to trip scoring and driver identification.

\n
FieldWhat it does
Eco Score Allowed EventsNumber of harsh-driving events (see Green Driving) tolerated within a trip before it affects the eco score for that trip.
Remember iButtonWhether the last-read iButton ID is retained and associated with the trip record, tying trips to a specific driver.
\n

11. I/O

The master list of every I/O element (AVL ID parameter) the device can report — GNSS/GSM status values, voltages, odometers, and all physical digital/analog inputs and outputs. Each row controls whether and how that specific parameter gets included in AVL records.

I/O tab — per-parameter table with Priority, Low/High Level thresholds, Event Only, Operand, and Avg Const columns, covering built-in status elements plus Digital/Analog Inputs and Outputs.

Table columns

Every row in the I/O table (Ignition, Movement, Data Mode, GSM Signal, Sleep Mode, GNSS Status, GNSS PDOP/HDOP, External Voltage, Speed, GSM Cell ID/Area Code, Battery Voltage/Current, Active GSM Operator, Trip/Total Odometer, Digital Inputs 1-4, Analog Inputs 1-4, Digital Outputs 1-2 and beyond) is controlled by the same set of columns.

\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
PriorityWhether this parameter can trigger its own event record, and at what priority — None (monitoring only, no dedicated event), Low, High, or Panic.
Low Level / High LevelThreshold values that define the trigger condition for Priority-based events — e.g. an External Voltage High Level triggers a high-voltage event.
Event OnlyYes records this parameter only when its own event fires; No means it's also included as regular monitoring data on every periodic record.
OperandHow the threshold is evaluated — Monitoring (no threshold logic, value just reported), or On Change (event fires whenever the value changes, common for binary-style parameters like Ignition/Movement).
Avg ConstAveraging constant applied to smooth noisy readings (e.g. voltages, PDOP/HDOP) before they're evaluated or reported — higher values smooth more aggressively.

Practical use

How this tab is actually used day to day.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Enabling a parameter for reportingSet its row's Priority away from None (or leave Event Only = No) so the value is included in outgoing AVL records at all.
Building a threshold-based eventSet Priority to the desired level, then set Low Level / High Level to the trigger range for that parameter.
Reducing data volumeLeave rarely-needed parameters (e.g. GSM Area Code) at Priority = None / Event Only = Yes so they don't bloat every periodic record.
Scope note: This table continues well beyond what's captured in the screenshot above (Digital/Analog Inputs 1-4, Digital Outputs, and additional CAN/vehicle-specific elements further down the list) — the column behavior described here applies uniformly to every row.

Part 2 — FMC650 CAN & Tachograph

Device note: Sections 12–15 were captured against an FMC650 profile (Configurator v4.41.0.0), which exposes a larger tab set than the FMB640 (adds EV FMS IO, Manual CAN, Bluetooth 4.0, Beacon List, Authorization ID List, Tachograph Data, RS232 \ RS485, CAN \ Tachograph, Transcan Advance, Euroscan IO). FMS IO and CAN \ Tachograph parameter behavior is broadly consistent across Teltonika's FMS-standard/tachograph-capable device range, but exact tab availability depends on the connected device's hardware and firmware.

12. FMS IO

The standardized FMS (Fleet Management System) parameter set decoded from the truck/bus's FMS-standard CAN bus — engine, fuel, and axle-weight data as defined by the FMS-standard interface most commercial vehicle manufacturers support. This is the primary source for CAN-based fuel and odometer reconciliation work.

FMS IO tab — FMS Fuel Settings at the top, followed by the full FMS IO parameter table (Brake switch, Wheel based speed, Engine data, Fuel Level, Axle weights, etc.).

FMS Fuel Settings

Chooses which upstream CAN standard supplies fuel data, and the unit resolution used for high-resolution totals — directly affects fuel-consumption investigation accuracy.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Fuel level sourceCAN (FMS-standard PGN) or J1708 — which bus protocol the Fuel Level percentage is read from.
Fuel Consumption sourceCAN or J1708 — same choice, applied to the fuel consumption/total-used values.
High resolution engine total fuel usedLiters or Milliliters — the unit granularity used when reporting the high-resolution total fuel counter.

FMS IO table

Same column structure as the standard I/O tab (Priority, Low/High Level, Event Only, Operand), applied here to FMS-standard vehicle CAN parameters instead of device-internal sensors.

\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Brake switch / Cruise control active / Clutch switch / PTO stateBoolean vehicle state flags read directly off the FMS CAN bus.
Wheel based speed (km/h)Vehicle speed as reported by the wheel sensors over CAN — often more accurate than GPS speed at low speed or in poor GNSS conditions, and the standard cross-check for GPS-vs-CAN speed/odometer reconciliation.
Accelerator pedal position / Engine percent load / Engine speed (RPM)Engine load and throttle data, useful for driver-behavior and duty-cycle analysis.
Engine total fuel used (liters) / Fuel Level (%)Cumulative fuel consumed and current tank level as reported by the ECU — the primary CAN-side fuel-investigation data source.
Axle 1-13+ weight (kg)Per-axle load sensor readings, where the vehicle supports it — used for overload detection and load-verification reporting.
Investigation use: Wheel based speed and Engine total fuel used are the two FMS parameters most often pulled directly into fuel and odometer reconciliation reports, since they come straight from the vehicle ECU rather than being GPS-derived.
\n

13. Manual CAN

Lets you manually define custom CAN frame decoding rules (up to dozens of user-defined "CAN0" – "CANxx" slots) for vehicles or CAN-connected equipment that don't fit the standard FMS parameter set — e.g. proprietary PGNs, refrigeration units, or non-FMS-compliant vehicles.

Manual CAN tab — one row per custom CAN slot (CAN0, CAN1, CAN2...), each with CAN Type, bit-level Data Mask, Operand, CAN ID, and CAN Source.

Per-row fields

Every custom CAN slot is configured independently with the same set of fields, letting you decode an arbitrary CAN ID/data-mask combination into a usable parameter.

\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
Can TypeDisabled, Standard (11-bit), or Extended (29-bit) — the CAN identifier frame format to listen for.
Data MaskBit-level selector (MSB to LSB across 8 bytes) picking exactly which bits of the CAN frame's payload are extracted as this parameter's value.
OperandHow the extracted value is evaluated/reported — typically Monitoring (reported as-is) or On Change.
Can IDThe specific CAN identifier (hex) this row listens for on the bus.
Can SourceWhich physical CAN bus (CAN1 or CAN2) this rule is applied to — matters on devices with dual CAN interfaces.
When to use this tab: Reach for Manual CAN when a vehicle's data isn't covered by the standard FMS IO parameter set — common with agricultural/construction equipment, refrigeration units on reefer trailers, or manufacturer-specific PGNs that need a DBC/PGN reference to decode correctly.
\n

14. Tachograph Data

Controls how digital tachograph data (driver cards, working states, VIN/VRN, speed/odometer as reported by the tachograph itself) is prioritized, filtered, and included in AVL records — separate from the underlying CAN1/CAN2 bus wiring configured on the CAN \ Tachograph tab.

Tachograph Data tab — Vehicle Data Priority Settings, Tachograph Settings, Driver Working State Filters, and the Tachograph Data parameter table.

Vehicle Data Priority Settings

When multiple onboard data sources are available (K Line, AllCan, TachoCan, FMS), this sets which takes priority for vehicle data resolution, and lets each be assigned its own priority tier.

FieldWhat it does
K Line Priority / AllCan Priority / TachoCan Priority / FMS PriorityDisable a source entirely, or assign it Priority 1 (highest) through Priority 4 (lowest) — determines which source's values win when more than one is reporting the same parameter.

Tachograph Settings

A single toggle controlling how tachograph data is packaged for transmission.

FieldWhat it does
Include Tachograph data into regular recordWhen enabled, tachograph parameters ride along in the device's normal periodic AVL records instead of only being sent as separate dedicated tachograph records.

Driver Working State Filters

Governs how driver working-state values behave around edge cases, particularly when ignition is off.

\n
FieldWhat it does
N/A driver stateDisable/Enable reporting of an explicit 'not available' working state when no valid state can be determined.
Deny driver work state when ignition offWhen enabled, suppresses working-state reporting while ignition is off, avoiding stale/misleading state values being logged during parked periods.

Tachograph Data table

Same Priority / Low-High Level / Event Only / Operand structure as other I/O tables, applied to tachograph-specific parameters.

\n\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
TimestampThe tachograph's own clock value, useful for cross-checking against device/GNSS time.
Drive recognize / OverspeedingTachograph-derived driving state and speed-limit-violation flags.
Vehicle Speed / Odometer / DistanceSpeed and mileage as reported by the tachograph — the counterpart to FMS IO's wheel-based speed, and another cross-check source for GPS-vs-CAN odometer reconciliation.
VIN / VRNVehicle Identification Number and Vehicle Registration Number read from the tachograph.
Driver 1/2 working state, card, time related states, identification numberPer-driver-slot data (the tachograph supports two driver card slots) covering current activity state, inserted card status, elapsed time in that state, and driver ID — the core dataset for driver-hours/compliance reporting.
\n

15. CAN \ Tachograph

The physical/protocol-level configuration for the device's CAN interfaces and the tachograph DDD (Driver Digital Data) file download process — this is where CAN bus speed, termination, and DDD download behavior actually get set, feeding the higher-level Tachograph Data and FMS IO tabs above.

CAN \\ Tachograph tab — CAN1/CAN2 Bus Settings, Tachograph Settings (DDD download source, ignition source), WEB Tacho Settings, and FMS Settings.

CAN1 / CAN2 Bus Settings

Low-level physical bus configuration for each of the device's two CAN interfaces — must match the vehicle's actual bus specification or no data will decode correctly.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
CAN bus speed (kbps)Bitrate of the bus (commonly 250 or 500 kbps on commercial vehicles) — must match the vehicle's actual CAN bus speed.
CAN bus modeSilent (passively listens only, never transmits/acknowledges — safest default for read-only telemetry) or Normal (actively participates on the bus, required for two-way DDD downloads).
CAN Termination ResistanceEnable the device's internal 120Ω termination resistor — only needed if the device sits at a physical end of the CAN bus and no other termination is present.

Tachograph Settings

Controls how the device pulls the DDD file (the digital tachograph's downloadable driver activity record) from the tachograph unit.

\n\n\n
FieldWhat it does
DDD download sourceWhich interface the device uses to request DDD data — CAN1, CAN2, Front Panel (the tachograph's front download port), or OFF.
Tachograph ignition sourceWhich input the tachograph download logic treats as ignition — Ignition, or DIN1–4.
Download alternative DDD card filesEnable/disable also downloading the driver card files (as opposed to only the vehicle unit file).
Auto DDD address selectionLet the device automatically resolve the tachograph's CAN address rather than requiring it to be set manually.

WEB Tacho Settings

A separate remote endpoint the device can push downloaded DDD files to directly, independent of the main telemetry server — used by dedicated tachograph-compliance platforms.

\n\n
FieldWhat it does
StatusEnable/disable WEB Tacho uploads.
Domain / PortAddress of the receiving WEB Tacho service.
Start delay (min.)Delay after device startup before the first WEB Tacho connection attempt.

FMS Settings

Tells the device which physical CAN bus carries the vehicle's FMS-standard traffic, feeding the FMS IO tab.

FieldWhat it does
FMS data sourceCAN1 or CAN2 — selects which bus the device listens on for FMS-standard PGNs.
How the tabs connect: CAN \ Tachograph sets the physical bus (speed/mode/termination) and DDD download mechanics; Tachograph Data then filters/prioritizes what gets reported from that download; FMS IO is a separate, standardized parameter set read off whichever bus is chosen as the FMS data source here.
Reference compiled from Teltonika Configurator v4.37.1.0 (FMB640) and v4.41.0.0 (FMC650). Always confirm exact tab availability and parameter behavior against the specific device profile in use before relying on this for a device outside these two models.
